prompts.display_text: Pin a continental Western European country (not Luxembourg or a microstate) that recognized the Church, 1952 to 1974
prompts.text_original: After World War II, the Church sought official legal standing from European governments so it could own property and operate freely. One of nine continental Western European countries (Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Belgium or the Netherlands) whose government officially recognized the Church between 1952 and 1974.
prompts.note: Switzerland (1864) and Italy (1993) recognized the Church outside these years, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: In the decades after World War II, Western European governments gave the Church legal standing one by one: France in 1952, West Germany in 1953, Austria and the Netherlands in 1955, Spain in 1968 and Portugal in 1974. Recognition let the Church own meetinghouses, hold meetings openly and bring in missionaries.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: West Germany recognized the Church as a public-law corporation, December 7, 1953.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France registered the Church as a foreign association in September 1952.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Spain officially recognized the Church, October 22, 1968.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Austria granted the Church legal recognition, September 27, 1955.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Netherlands recognized the Church, August 22, 1955, after 19 years of requests.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: David M. Kennedy secured official recognition in Lisbon in 1974.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory outside the US where President Hinckley met Saints on his 2005 round-the-world trip
prompts.text_original: In July and August 2005, at age 95, President Gordon B. Hinckley flew around the world, stopping to meet Saints in seven cities. A country or territory outside the United States where he stopped to meet members or dedicate a building on that trip.
prompts.citation: Liahona, Dec. 2005, President Hinckley Travels the World
prompts.note: Hong Kong is the answer for the Hong Kong stop; mainland China was not visited.
prompts.summary: In mid-2005 President Gordon B. Hinckley, then 95, circled the globe. He greeted Saints at Vladivostok, spoke in Seoul, dedicated office buildings in Taipei and Hong Kong, dedicated the Aba Nigeria Temple, and met small groups of members in Delhi and Nairobi.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: He spoke at a regional conference in Seoul marking 50 years of the Church in Korea.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: He dedicated the Aba Nigeria Temple.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: He greeted about 200 members at the Vladivostok airport during a refueling stop.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: He met members in Hong Kong and dedicated a Church office building.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: He met members in Taipei and dedicated a Church office building.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: He met a small group of members in Delhi during a brief stop.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: He met a small group of members in Nairobi during a brief stop.

prompts.display_text: Pin an Asian or Pacific country or territory where a current General Authority Seventy was born (October 2026, not US states).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies were born in Asia or the Pacific islands. Pin a country or territory there where a current General Authority Seventy was born, according to the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.note: Elder J. Kimo Esplin was born in Kahuku, Hawaii, a US state, so the display rules out US states.
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, current General Authority Seventies were born in the Philippines, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Tonga and Fiji. Elder Benjamin M. Z. Tai of Hong Kong serves in the Presidency of the Seventy.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Elders Revillo (General Santos City), Fantone (Manila) and Teh (Davao City).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Elder Takashi Wada, born in Nagano.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Elders Christopher H. Kim (Daegu) and Yoon Hwan Choi (Seoul).

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Elders Chi Hong (Sam) Wong and Benjamin M. Z. Tai of the Presidency of the Seventy.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Elder Vaiangina Sikahema, born in Nuku'alofa.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Elder Taniela B. Wakolo, born in Lomaloma, Lau.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Elder Wan-Liang Wu, born in Taipei.
